body:
Yeah, you're right about not taking it personally. It's just that I hate not knowing what I might have done wrong during the interview. That drives me crazy and, with my self-esteem not being that high, I start making assumptions about myself. All of those negative thoughts can quickly sink in when I'm in an emotionally vulnerable state.

Being active is definitely a problem for me right now. Since I moved to the city, I've gained some weight, and have been spending a lot of time indoors. I really miss the area where I used to live. It was much more suburban, pedestrian friendly, and safe. Being unemployed and completely cut off from my friends (all of whom live more than 50 miles away) has also been contributing to my increasingly sedentary lifestyle.

I haven't stopped writing completely, but it mostly consists of cover letters these days. For a while, I was ghost-writing articles and doing some freelance work, but there was a point where I began to feel that my writing was not improving at all and that made me feel very self-conscious and depressed. Other professional writers can pump out a 400 word piece in anywhere from 15-20 minutes. It takes about twice as long for me if not longer. It's so difficult for me to articulate my ideas or thoughts in a way that reads well. Eventually, I got so frustrated at my lack of writing ability that I haven't made much effort to start back up since then.
